# EVALUATION CRITERIA

## Evaluation at a Glance
- **Award Method:** Competitive Sealed Bids (Firm Fixed Price) awarded to the responsible Bidder submitting a responsive Bid with the most favorable (lowest) Total Bid Price. In the event of a tie in Total Bid Price, award is based on the Bidder with the strongest demonstrated experience and qualifications as documented in required reference submissions.
- **Total Available Points / Weight:** Not specified in RFP
- **Technical Minimum Threshold:** Not specified in RFP
- **Financial / Price Threshold:** Not specified in RFP
- **Evaluation Stages:** Not specified in RFP

## 1. Technical Evaluation Criteria

### Demonstrated Experience and Qualifications (Tie-Breaker Criterion)
- **What is assessed:** Evaluation of Bidder's experience and qualifications as documented in required reference submissions, used solely in the event of a tie in Total Bid Price.
- **Weight / Points:** Not specified in RFP
- **Evidence expected:** Documentation of at least three (3) reference contracts of similar scope and complexity (minimum 500,000 identities) within the last three (3) years, including contact name, phone number, email address, and a brief description of services provided.
- **Scoring notes:** Evaluated at MHBE's sole discretion to award the Contract in the event of a tie in Total Bid Price; MHBE may request additional information to resolve a tie.
- **Source:** Addendum.pdf • Page 5 • Section 7.0 AMENDMENTS TO SECTION 5 – BASIS FOR AWARD

## 2. Financial Evaluation Criteria

### Total Bid Price
- **What is assessed:** Total cost to provide the required PingOne Advanced Identity Cloud subscription licenses, support package, training, onboarding, professional services, and sandbox environments as specified in Section 2.2.
- **Weight / Points:** Not specified in RFP
- **Evaluation method:** Lowest Total Bid Price calculated on IFB Attachment D - Bid Form submitted by a responsible Bidder with a responsive Bid.
- **Pricing evidence required:** Completed Attachment D - Bid Price Form with all unit and extended prices filled in dollars and cents, including Line Item 16 entered as $0.00, signed and dated by an authorized representative.
- **Source:** 364_rfp_PingOne_Advanced_Identity_Subscription_IFB_BPM057272_FINAL.pdf • Page 14 • SECTION 5 — BASIS FOR AWARD

## 3. Mandatory Requirements (Pass / Fail)

### Reseller Letter of Authorization
- **Requirement:** Bidder must submit with the bid a letter of authorization from the manufacturer (PingIdentity) providing evidence of the rights to resell all products and services required by this IFB.
- **Consequence if unmet:** Bids will be deemed non-responsive if no minimum qualification documentation is submitted.
- **Source:** 364_rfp_PingOne_Advanced_Identity_Subscription_IFB_BPM057272_FINAL.pdf • Page 10 • SECTION 3 – BIDDER MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

### Minimum Reseller Experience
- **Requirement:** Bidder must have been an authorized PingIdentity reseller for a minimum of two (2) years prior to the closing date of this IFB.
- **Consequence if unmet:** Bid will be determined non-responsive and rejected by MHBE.
- **Source:** Addendum.pdf • Page 4 • Section 5.0 AMENDMENTS TO SECTION 3 – BIDDER MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

### Reference Contracts Documentation
- **Requirement:** Bidder must submit documentation of at least three (3) reference contracts of similar scope and complexity (minimum 500,000 identities) within the last three (3) years, including contact name, phone number, email address, and a brief description of services provided.
- **Consequence if unmet:** Bid will be determined non-responsive and rejected by MHBE.
- **Source:** Addendum.pdf • Page 4 • Section 5.0 AMENDMENTS TO SECTION 3 – BIDDER MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

SECTION 1 — BACKGROUND 
 
2.5 Background on the Affordable Care Act 
 
The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (“MHBE”) is an independent unit of State government 
established to provide Maryland’s residents and small businesses with the opportunity to compare 
rates, benefits, and quality among health insurance plans and to facilitate individuals’ enrollment in 
plans that best suit their needs. MHBE also evaluates eligibility for expanded Medicaid coverage, 
advanced premium tax credits (“APTC”) and other cost-sharing programs designed to make coverage 
more affordable for individuals with household incomes below 400 percent of the federal poverty level 
(“FPL”). 
 
1.2 Background on Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Procurement  
 
Under § 31-103 of the Insurance Article of the Maryland Code, the MHBE is subject to the provisions of 
State law governing procurement by “exempt units.” See Md. Code Ann., State Fin. & Proc. § 12-401.  
The principal body that oversees MHBE procurements is the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Board of 
Trustees.  This procurement method is Competitive Sealed Bidding (Firm Fixed Price) as allowed under II. 
A. of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Procurement Policies and Procedures, which the Board of 
Trustees adopted in a resolution dated June 27, 2011.  
1.3 Federal Funding Acknowledgement 
 
This procurement contains federal funds from the following source: Medicaid Funds, CFDA number 
93.778.  Execution of a Contract awarded as a result of this bid indicates the Contractor’s agreement 
with all federal funding terms and conditions that apply to contractors receiving federal funds from 
these sources, including the applicable provisions described in Attachment E.

the Key Information Summary Sheet. The name of each Bidder, the Total Bid Price, and such

1.5 Confidentiality of Bids

# ADDENDUM CHANGE SUMMARY

## WHAT CHANGED
- **Proposal Submission Deadline**: Extended from July 16, 2026 at 11:00 AM EST to August 13, 2026 at 11:00 AM EST across all submission deliverables and criteria.
- **New Deliverables Added**:
  - Amendment No. 1 Acknowledgement Form (signed written acknowledgement submitted with bid).
  - eMMA Amendment Acknowledgement (electronic acknowledgement in eMMA portal).
  - Reference Documentation (documentation of at least 3 reference contracts of similar scope/complexity, min 500,000 identities, within the last 3 years).
  - Pre-Bid Conference Presentation Delivery (1-hour remote pre-bid presentation and recording provided post-award).
- **New Mandatory Evaluation & Qualification Requirements**:
  - Minimum of 2 years as an authorized PingIdentity reseller prior to IFB closing date.
  - Required 3 reference contract submissions added as a mandatory pass/fail threshold and tie-breaker criterion for Total Bid Price ties.
- **Risk Assessment**: High → Medium.
- **Final Decision**: NO-GO → MAYBE (the extended deadline reopened the bid window, removing the automatic NO-GO override for a passed submission date).

## OVERALL IMPACT
This amendment extends the submission deadline to August 13, 2026, and adds strict reseller experience and reference documentation requirements, shifting the final recommendation from NO-GO to MAYBE as the proposal window is now open for evaluation.

SECTION 1 — BACKGROUND 
 
2.5 Background on the Affordable Care Act 
 
The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (“MHBE”) is an independent unit of State government 
established to provide Maryland’s residents and small businesses with the opportunity to compare 
rates, benefits, and quality among health insurance plans and to facilitate individuals’ enrollment in 
plans that best suit their needs. MHBE also evaluates eligibility for expanded Medicaid coverage, 
advanced premium tax credits (“APTC”) and other cost-sharing programs designed to make coverage 
more affordable for individuals with household incomes below 400 percent of the federal poverty level 
(“FPL”). 
 
1.2 Background on Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Procurement  
 
Under § 31-103 of the Insurance Article of the Maryland Code, the MHBE is subject to the provisions of 
State law governing procurement by “exempt units.” See Md. Code Ann., State Fin. & Proc. § 12-401.  
The principal body that oversees MHBE procurements is the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Board of 
Trustees.  This procurement method is Competitive Sealed Bidding (Firm Fixed Price) as allowed under II. 
A. of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Procurement Policies and Procedures, which the Board of 
Trustees adopted in a resolution dated June 27, 2011.  
1.3 Federal Funding Acknowledgement

93.778.  Execution of a Contract awarded as a result of this bid indicates the Contractor’s agreement 
with all federal funding terms and conditions that apply to contractors receiving federal funds from 
these sources, including the applicable provisions described in Attachment E.

time and date set for Bid opening. Before Bid opening, the State may not disclose the identity of 
any Bidder.

the Key Information Summary Sheet. The name of each Bidder, the Total Bid Price, and such 
other information as is deemed appropriate shall be published on MHBE’S website upon award.

# ADDENDUM CHANGE SUMMARY

## WHAT CHANGED
- **Proposal Submission Closing Date:** Extended from July 16, 2026, at 11:00 AM EST → July 21, 2026, at 11:00 AM EST.
- **Pre-Bid Conference Date:** Updated from Tuesday, July 7, 2026 → Wednesday, July 8, 2026, at 1:00 PM EST.
- **Bidder Minimum Qualifications:** Added requirement for a minimum of two (2) years as an authorized PingIdentity reseller prior to the bid due date, verified by a formal statement from PingIdentity confirming the authorization date.
- **New Submission Deliverable — Transmittal Letter Addenda Statement & Acknowledgment Form:** Added mandatory requirement to include a statement in the Transmittal Letter acknowledging receipt of all addenda (specifically Addendum No. 1) and submit the Addendum No. 1 Acknowledgment Form.
- **Revised Bid Price Form (Attachment D):** Updated Attachment D pricing instructions requiring Line Item #16 (Free Sandbox) to be entered at exactly $0.00; entering any non-zero price is now an explicit disqualification trigger.
- **New Delivery Deliverable — Support Entitlement Coordination:** Added requirement to coordinate with PingIdentity prior to September 1, 2026, to ensure MHBE's support entitlements are active and verified.
- **New Invoicing Requirement:** Added mandate that all post-award invoices must explicitly list applicable PingIdentity product code(s) and the corresponding purchase order number.

## OVERALL IMPACT
This amendment extends the submission timeline, adds a 2-year minimum reseller experience qualification, and mandates strict pricing ($0.00 for Line Item #16) and addenda acknowledgment requirements. SECTION 1 — BACKGROUND 
 
2.5 Background on the Affordable Care Act 
 
The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (“MHBE”) is an independent unit of State government 
established to provide Maryland’s residents and small businesses with the opportunity to compare 
rates, benefits, and quality among health insurance plans and to facilitate individuals’ enrollment in 
plans that best suit their needs. MHBE also evaluates eligibility for expanded Medicaid coverage, 
advanced premium tax credits (“APTC”) and other cost-sharing programs designed to make coverage 
more affordable for individuals with household incomes below 400 percent of the federal poverty level 
(“FPL”). 
 
1.2 Background on Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Procurement  
 
Under § 31-103 of the Insurance Article of the Maryland Code, the MHBE is subject to the provisions of 
State law governing procurement by “exempt units.” See Md. Code Ann., State Fin. & Proc. § 12-401.  
The principal body that oversees MHBE procurements is the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Board of 
Trustees.  This procurement method is Competitive Sealed Bidding (Firm Fixed Price) as allowed under II. 
A. of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Procurement Policies and Procedures, which the Board of 
Trustees adopted in a resolution dated June 27, 2011.  
1.3 Federal Funding Acknowledgement 
 
This procurement contains federal funds from the following source: Medicaid Funds, CFDA number 
93.778.  Execution of a Contract awarded as a result of this bid indicates the Contractor’s agreement 
with all federal funding terms and conditions that apply to contractors receiving federal funds from 
these sources, including the applicable provisions described in Attachment E. 
1.4 Receipt, Opening and Recording of Bids 
1.4.1 Upon receipt, each Bid and any timely modification(s) to a Bid shall remain unopened until the 
time and date set for Bid opening. Before Bid opening, the State may not disclose the identity of 
any Bidder. 
1.4.2  Bids and timely modifications to Bids shall be opened at the time, date and place set forth in 
the Key Information Summary Sheet. The name of each Bidder, the Total Bid Price, and such 
other information as is deemed appropriate shall be published on MHBE’S website upon award.  
1.5 Confidentiality of Bids 
1.5.1 The Bids shall be tabulated, or a Bid abstract made. The opened Bids shall be available for public 
inspection at a reasonable time after Bid opening, but in any case, before Contract award, 
except to the extent the Bidder designates trade secrets or other proprietary data to be 
confidential as set forth in this solicitation. See Sections 1.6, 4.1.3 for further information.
